
```{r setup}
library(epicurves)
set.seed(1)
```

This vignette reproduces the simulation study and real-data application of
Article 1 (the SIRD-GA model) using only exported functions of this
package.

## Basic reproduction number and ODE mass balance

```{r r0}
sird_R0(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.15, alpha = 0.08)
out <- sird_ode_solve(times = 0:200, x0 = c(s = 0.999, i = 0.001, r = 0),
                       parms = list(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.15, alpha = 0.08))
range(out$s + out$i + out$r + out$d) # should be 1 throughout
```

## Simulation study

```{r sim}
N <- 20000
theta_true <- c(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.15, alpha = 0.08, s0 = 0.999, i0 = 0.001,
                 r0 = 0, p = 0.6, tau2 = 0.2)
sim <- sird_ga_simulate_obs(N, S0 = round(N * 0.999), I0 = round(N * 0.001), R0 = 0,
                             lambda = theta_true[["lambda"]], gamma = theta_true[["gamma"]],
                             alpha = theta_true[["alpha"]], p = theta_true[["p"]],
                             tau2 = theta_true[["tau2"]], Tmax = 100, Delta = 1)

fit <- sird_ga_fit(sim$y, N, Delta = 1,
                    start = list(lambda = 0.3, gamma = 0.1, alpha = 0.1, i0 = 0.002,
                                 p = 0.5, tau2 = 0.3),
                    n_sub = 6, hessian = FALSE, control = list(maxit = 1000, reltol = 1e-9))
round(fit$theta, 4)
sird_R0(fit$theta[["lambda"]], fit$theta[["gamma"]], fit$theta[["alpha"]])
```

Transmission rate and $R_0$ recover well; the recovery/mortality split
($\gamma$ vs. $\alpha$) is only partially identified from infection-only
data, consistent with the thesis's own appendix simulation (Scenarios 4-5),
where the sum $\gamma+\alpha$ is recovered far more precisely than either
rate individually.

## Real-data application: COVID-19 first wave, Paraíba, Brazil

```{r real-data}
data(paraiba_covid19)
data(paraiba_population)
y_raw <- paraiba_covid19$new_cases
y_smooth <- smooth_series(y_raw, 7)
```

Raw daily case counts carry pronounced day-of-week reporting artefacts
(lower weekend counts, Monday catch-up spikes) that materially affect the
Kalman-filter likelihood surface; `smooth_series()` applies a 7-day
centered moving average before estimation, as recommended for this
application.

```{r real-fit}
fit_real <- sird_ga_fit(
  y_smooth, paraiba_population, Delta = 1,
  start = list(lambda = 0.26, gamma = 0.23, alpha = 0.02, i0 = 1e-4, p = 0.93, tau2 = 0.67^2),
  p_max = 0.98, n_sub = 6, hessian = FALSE, control = list(maxit = 2000, reltol = 1e-11)
)
round(fit_real$theta, 4)
sird_R0(fit_real$theta[["lambda"]], fit_real$theta[["gamma"]], fit_real$theta[["alpha"]])

kf_real <- sird_ga_loglik(fit_real$theta, y_smooth, paraiba_population, Delta = 1,
                           n_sub = 6, keep_states = TRUE)
plot_sird_ga_fit(y_smooth, kf_real)
```

## A practical-identifiability finding

Starting the optimiser at the published parameter point
($\lambda=0.26,\gamma=0.23,\alpha=0.02,p=0.93,\tau=0.67$) yields a
log-likelihood almost as high as the value found by unconstrained search
from a diffuse starting point, indicating a flat ridge in the likelihood
surface along which $\lambda$ and $\gamma+\alpha$ trade off while preserving
$R_0$ and the shape of the fitted curve. This is a known weak-identifiability
feature of SIR/SIRD models estimated from incidence-only series (the
transmission and removal rates are identified mainly through their ratio and
through the curve's inflection timing, not independently), and is reported
as a limitation in Article 1's discussion rather than concealed. We
recommend reporting a profile likelihood or a multi-start sensitivity
analysis alongside any single point estimate for this application.
